meta.title: Budget Tracker specification
meta.product: A personal / household budget tracker. A budget starts from the monthly total of its incomes, is split into categories and subcategories with a monthly expectation each, and is tracked period by period against the transactions the user records. It also tracks subscriptions, debts, and the planned flow of money between accounts. CHF only. UI in English and French.

glossary.definition: The container of everything else: incomes, categories, subscriptions, debts, transactions, periods and accounts. Always a monthly budget.
The member who created the budget. Only the owner can delete it, change its end date, or manage members and invitations.
A person who belongs to a budget (the owner included). Every member can read and edit everything in the budget.
An offer to join a budget, addressed by the owner to an email address. The invited person accepts or declines it after signing in with a matching verified email.
A monthly amount with a nominal pay day, belonging to one member of the budget. The incomes of a budget sum into its monthly total.
The one income of a budget whose pay dates define the periods.
The day of the month an income is due, for example the 25th, before clamping to the month length and before the weekend rule.
The date an income is really paid in a given month: the nominal pay day clamped to the month length, then moved by the weekend rule (or overridden by hand).
Per income: how a pay day that falls on a Saturday or Sunday moves. One of nearest (default), previous, next, none.
The span from one actual pay date of the primary income to the day before the next one. A stored row with a start and an end date.
The period that contains today. The last period that exists as a row; its end date is a projection.
The point between the end of one period and the start of the next. It can be moved by hand; a manual boundary is never recomputed.
The current period end computed as the day before the next actual pay date of the primary income.
The 1-based number of a period within its budget. Income validity and versions refer to it, not to dates.
An income is in force in a period when it started at or before that period and has not ended before it; a version is in force when it is the latest one effective at or before that period.
Of a period: the sum of the incomes in force in that period, each at the version in force for that period.
The sum of all incomes of the budget; the amount the budget starts from.
The terms of an income (and later of a category expectation, a subscription or a debt) in force from a given period on. Edits create versions; they never rewrite the past.
The first level of the budget split, for example insurance. Holds the monthly expectation when it has no subcategories.
The optional second (and last) level under a category, for example insurance/car.
The amount planned for a category or subcategory per month, entered per month or per year.
Of a period: its income total minus the sum of the expectations in force in that period. Negative when more is assigned than the income.
What is left of a category within a period. Reset at the end of each period.
The surplus or deficit of a period: its income total minus the total spent in it. Per category: the expectation minus what was spent.
An amount on a date, in a category or subcategory, with an optional description and an optional link to a debt or a subscription.
A recurring charge with a price, a first charge date, a cadence (monthly, quarterly, half-yearly or yearly) and a category.
When a subscription will next be charged.
Money owed, with a principal, an optional interest rate and a planned monthly payment.
What is still owed on a debt; transactions assigned to the debt reduce it.
A place money is kept (salary account, savings, third pillar, tax reserve), possibly at different banks.

A planned movement of money between two accounts, scheduled as an offset in days from an income's actual pay date (such as "payday + 2 days: 1000 CHF from A to Savings") or on a fixed day of the month. Flagged automatic or manual.
A planned transfer done by a standing order; assumed done.
A planned transfer the user makes by hand; shown as a per-period checklist.
The plan of transfers between accounts after payday, drawn as a diagram.
Bulk creation of transactions through the one import function in the database, from a paste/CSV screen, a repository script a Claude session can run, and later a connector.
The mark an imported transaction carries until the user has checked it.
A saved mapping from a merchant to a category, so categorisation of imports improves over time.
The hundredth of a Swiss franc (centime). Every amount is an integer number of rappen.
Swiss franc, the only currency.
The calendar date in Europe/Zurich, decided by the database.
A day written YYYY-MM-DD (Postgres date): not an instant, never converted through a time zone.
An instant with a time and a zone (Postgres timestamptz), shown as the local calendar date of that instant.
The point where money or dates enter or leave the app as text: display and input. Formatting and parsing happen only there.
Postgres policies deciding which rows each user may read or change. The only access control of the app.
The state after a password-recovery link signed a user in: they must choose a new password before using the app. Tied to that exact sign-in.
A link Supabase Auth sends by email (sign-up confirmation, password recovery, email change) that brings the user back to the app with a session or an error.
Email-link tokens kept for one tab (sessionStorage, never a URL) after their check failed for a transient reason, so a reload retries.
The identity of one sign-in: the session_id claim of the access token, or the user id when there is none.
The Supabase anon key meant for the browser. With the project URL, the only configuration that reaches the browser.
The name a user chooses at sign-up, kept in their profile.
One row per user, created on sign-up, with their display name and email.
The home page of the app: the current period at a glance.

actors.description: Anyone signed in, before or regardless of belonging to a given budget. Relative to a budget they are not a member of, they are "another user" and can see or change nothing in it.

actors.name: budget owner
actors.description: The member who created a budget. Everything a member can do, plus delete the budget, change its end date, and manage members and invitations.

actors.name: budget member
actors.description: A person who belongs to a budget, the owner included unless stated. Reads and edits everything in the budget.

actors.name: invited person

rules.statement: A signed-in user sees the app shell: the sidebar navigation and the page they opened.
An unknown path shows a "page not found" page.
The app refuses to start without its Supabase settings and names the missing variables.
A refused or failed database call is shown as a translated message: each stable error code of the contract has its own text, and anything else a generic one; the raw error is never shown.
After a write fails, the data it acted on is read again, so a row that changed or disappeared meanwhile is never left on screen.

When a dialog closes (cancelled, dismissed or saved), keyboard focus returns to what opened it; for a dialog opened from a row's menu, to that row's menu button, and to the page's heading when that row is gone.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A write is sent once: submitting the same form again (or clicking again) while its write is in flight sends nothing more, however fast it happens.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The UI is available in English and in French.
The UI language the user chooses is remembered in the browser and set as the page language.
CHF is the only currency.
rules.rationale: Nothing in the data model carries a currency, so a test cannot prove the absence of a second one.

rules.statement: Money amounts are stored as integer rappen (centimes), never as floats.
Money is displayed with Swiss formatting.
Dates are displayed as dd.mm.yyyy.
A signed-out visitor who opens an app page is sent to sign-in, and back to the page they asked for once signed in.
A signed-in user who opens the sign-in or sign-up page is sent on into the app.
The page to return to after sign-in is always an in-app path, never an auth page and never another site.
Sign-up asks for a display name, an email address and a password, and stores the display name with the new account.
A new password has at least 8 characters.
A display name is required and has at most 80 characters.
When the account needs email confirmation, sign-up tells the user to check their inbox instead of signing them in.
When sign-up returns a session, the user goes straight into the app.
Sign-in validates the email and password fields before calling Supabase.
The email address is submitted trimmed.
An error from Supabase Auth is shown as a translated message, never as the raw error.
A confirmation (non-recovery) email link signs the user straight in.
Email-link tokens are removed from the address bar and from browser history: the token-bearing history entry is replaced, not followed by a new one.
An expired, used or invalid email link is explained, with a way to request a new confirmation email or a new password-reset link.
When sign-in fails because the email is not confirmed, the app offers to resend the confirmation email, with the address filled in.
The new-password form shows only while recovery mode is active for the signed-in session (invariant A).
The new-password form names the account whose password it changes (invariant A).
In recovery mode every app page leads to the new-password form, wherever the link landed, until the password is saved or the user signs out (invariant A).
The outcome of an email link that just landed is never discarded because another session exists (invariant B).
An email link never falls through to the new-password form for a different account (invariant B).

Parked link tokens and the recovery flag belong to one user and one attempt: they are dropped on a definite answer, on sign-out, when the user dismisses the notice, and when another sign-in takes over (invariant C).
When an email link cannot be checked for a transient reason, it is kept for this tab only, never in a URL, and reloading the tab retries it.
Signing in with a password ends recovery mode (invariant D).
Every state of the reset-password page has one consistent message and one way on (invariant E).
One user's cached data is never shown to another: the query cache is cleared when the signed-in user changes or signs out, and kept across a token refresh of the same user.

When a valid email link for one account is opened while another account is signed in, the app says that the browser is now signed in as the link's account, and that the other account was signed out here.
The new-password form is emptied whenever the signed-in user changes, so text typed for one account is never saved as another account's password.
Every user has a profile, created when they sign up.
A user can change only their own display name, and no other column of their profile.
A user can read their own profile and the profiles of people who share a budget with them now, and no others.
All access control is row-level security in Postgres.
rules.rationale: The browser talks to Supabase directly, so RLS is the only line of defence.

rules.statement: A user sees and changes only the data of budgets they are a member of.
An anonymous visitor can read or change no budget data.
A request for a budget, income, period or invitation the caller cannot see is answered as "not found", never as "forbidden".
Claude does not get raw database access to real data.

rules.statement: Everything else (incomes, categories, subscriptions, debts, transactions, periods, accounts) belongs to exactly one budget.
The creator of a budget is its owner.
The owner is a member of the budget, assigned by default when it is created.
A user can belong to several budgets.
A budget runs indefinitely or until an end date.
A budget is always a monthly budget.
An end date only stops period generation.
A budget's end is the end date the owner entered: no period starts after it, and the period containing it is the last one and ends at its normal end, which is the end shown.
Budgets can be created, modified and deleted.
Creating a budget is one atomic step that also creates its first income, as the primary income, and its first period.
A budget never exists without an income and a period.
A user can own at most 20 budgets.
An end date can be set at most ten years ahead.
A signed-in user who belongs to no budget is shown the first-run setup (create a budget, or accept an invitation addressed to them) instead of the app pages.

The budget a user works in is remembered for that user in this browser, also when it was chosen for them as a fallback, so a rename elsewhere never moves them to another budget; when it is no longer one of theirs (deleted, left, or they were removed), the app moves to another of their budgets, or to the first-run setup when none is left.
Deleting a budget asks the owner to type the budget's name first.
Every member can read and edit everything in the budget.
Only the owner can delete the budget.
Only the owner can change the budget's end date.
Only the owner can manage members and invitations.
A member can leave a budget.
The owner cannot leave the budget; they delete it instead.
Removing a member, or a member leaving, ends their incomes from the current period.
Past periods keep the incomes of a member who was removed or left.
A member whose income is the primary income cannot be removed until another income is made primary.
A budget has at most 20 members.

The app offers owner-only actions (change the end date, delete the budget, invite, cancel an invitation, remove a member) only to the owner; a plain member is told that only the owner can do them. The database still enforces this on its own.
The owner adds people to a budget by inviting an email address.
The app sends no email for an invitation.
The invited person sees the invitation after signing in with an account whose verified email matches the invited address, and not otherwise.
The invited person accepts or declines an unexpired invitation.
Inviting never reveals whether an address has an account.
A budget has at most 20 pending invitations.
A budget has at least one income.
Any member can add, edit and remove any income of the budget, including one that belongs to another member; a new income belongs to the member who adds it unless they choose another member.
source: owner-request: product owner decision on Q-001, 2026-11-15

rules.statement: All incomes of the budget sum into the budget's monthly total.
An income has an amount and a nominal pay day of the month.
Each income has its own weekend rule; the default is `nearest`.
Exactly one income of the budget is the primary income.
The primary income defines the periods.
The primary income can be switched to another income.
The last income of a budget cannot be removed.
Incomes are monthly.
Each income in force counts once per period, whatever its own pay day.

Removing an income that has already counted in a past period ends it from the current period instead of deleting it (unless the removal is an explicit correction from an earlier period, R-INCOME-015).
A budget has at most 50 incomes in force; ended incomes do not count.
An income amount is from 1 rappen to CHF 10 million (1 000 000 000 rappen).
The database lets any member of a budget add an income for another member and change or remove another member's income.
source: owner-request: product owner decision on Q-001, 2026-11-15

rules.statement: With the weekend rule `nearest`, a pay day that falls on a Saturday is paid the Friday before.
With the weekend rule `nearest`, a pay day that falls on a Sunday is paid the Monday after.
With the weekend rule `previous`, a pay day that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is paid the Friday before.
With the weekend rule `next`, a pay day that falls on a Saturday or a Sunday is paid the Monday after.
With the weekend rule `none`, a pay day is paid on its day even on a weekend.
A pay day of 29, 30 or 31 is clamped to the last day of shorter months before the weekend rule is applied.
The weekend rule is one of `nearest`, `previous`, `next` and `none`.
A period starts on the actual (weekend-adjusted) pay date of the primary income.
rules.rationale: Example with a nominal 25th: if 25 January is a Saturday, the period starts Friday 24 January.

rules.statement: A period ends the day before the next period starts; by default, the day before the next pay date given by the projection rule (R-PERIOD-030).
The salary (the primary income) is always day one of its period.
Periods are stored rows with a start and an end date.
The periods of a budget are contiguous.
The periods of a budget never overlap.
Past periods are not recomputed when the income's pay day later changes.
Only periods up to the current one exist as rows.
Periods are created on demand.
The current period's end date is a projection: the day before the next pay date given by the projection rule, unless set by hand.
When the primary income's terms change or another income becomes primary, the current period's end is re-projected unless it was set by hand, and never to a date before today.
The user can move the boundary between two existing periods to a date up to today, to match when a salary really arrived; moving it back undoes it.
rules.rationale: Public holidays.

rules.statement: The user can set the date the next salary is expected (after today): the current period, including the final period of a budget with an end date, ends the day before.
rules.rationale: Public holidays.

rules.statement: A manual boundary is never overwritten by recomputation.
When creating a budget the user chooses the month to start tracking from; the default is the current period.
The month to start tracking from can be earlier than the current period.
rules.rationale: So that past transactions can be entered.

rules.statement: "Today" is the calendar date in Europe/Zurich, decided by the database, not by the browser's clock or UTC.
A period's income total is the sum of the incomes in force in that period, each at the version in force for that period, plus the extra incomes dated in it.
A budget can start tracking at most 60 months back.
Every period is 7 to 92 days long; boundary operations that would break this are refused.
When a budget is opened, the app asks the database to create its missing periods (ensure_periods) and refreshes what depends on them when any were created.
An edit to an income's terms creates a new version effective from the current period.
source: domain: Versioning: edits never rewrite the past

rules.statement: An edit to a category expectation creates a new version effective from the current period.
source: domain: Versioning: edits never rewrite the past

rules.statement: An edit to a subscription's terms (price, cadence, category, schedule) creates a new version effective from the current period; charges already created never change.
source: domain: Versioning: edits never rewrite the past

rules.statement: An edit to a category expectation can, as an explicit "correct an earlier period" choice, apply from an earlier period instead of the current one.
rules.rationale: The same optional correction as for incomes (D-065); like an income correction, it applies until the next existing change (D-084).

rules.retiredBecause: Switching the primary income can no longer close or move a period (R-PERIOD-029), so it needs no confirmation; the app reports the next pay date the database then expects (R-INCOME-054).

rules.statement: Writing a version for a period discards the versions keyed to later periods, so terms just saved hold from that period on and are never shadowed.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15
rules.retiredBecause: Nothing is keyed beyond the latest period any more (R-VERSION-011, D-083), so there are no later versions to discard.

rules.statement: An income's terms can be corrected from an earlier period of the income, as an explicit correction; normal edits never change past periods.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

rules.statement: A change of terms (an edit, a correction, switching the primary income) never moves a stored boundary; its only effect on periods is to re-project the current period's end when it was not set by hand.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The next pay date after a period is the first actual pay date of the primary income, under the terms in force, at least 15 days after the period's start (and, when re-projecting after a change of terms, after today).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget can never get stuck: creating the missing periods always succeeds, each starting the day after the previous one ends, until one contains today or the budget's end is reached.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every write first creates the missing periods up to today, then acts.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The expected next pay date set by hand can be reset to the projection.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: When the salary arrives early, the current period closes and the next one starts on the day it arrived (today or earlier).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Nothing is keyed beyond the latest period: when the latest period is merged into the previous one, everything keyed to it is re-keyed to the previous period, the later write winning, so a change made now is in force now.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A correction from an earlier period applies from that period until the next existing change; later versions are left alone.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Only an income in force in the current period can become the primary income.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: After the primary income's terms change or another income becomes primary, the app says when the next salary is now expected, as read back from the database.

Before new pay terms of the primary income are saved, and before another income is made primary, the app shows the expected next pay date that would result, from the database's preview, and Save waits for it; an end set by hand is said to stay as set. The previewed end goes back with the save, which is refused if the period would now end on another day.
source: owner-request: coordinator, frontend adaptation to the step 3 database review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every place that announces the primary income's next salary (the dashboard, the income card, the periods page, the message after saving, the previews before saving) gives the same date, the day after the current period ends (projected or set by hand), never the schedule's next pay date; in the budget's last period it announces the budget's end instead, and an ended budget announces none. Another income's card shows its own next pay date only while the budget runs and not after its end.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Accepting, declining, cancelling and re-sending an invitation never deadlock with each other.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the second step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: When the latest period is merged into the previous one, what was keyed to the merged period always wins over what the previous period had for the same record, so the terms in force before the reopen are still in force after it.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A table keyed to periods is checked when it registers for merges, and a merge never fails because a row that would never be in force is referenced by other rows (it is kept as a void row).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Before reopening, a member can list everything the reopen would move into the previous period, for every kind of record, and what it would replace.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Before saving, a member can see what the current period's end and expected next pay date would become under proposed terms (a correction from an earlier period included) or a proposed primary income: the preview takes the write's arguments and is computed exactly as the write does, and the write can be refused when its result no longer matches the preview.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A member removed (or leaving) after the budget ended has their incomes end from the first period created if the budget resumes.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: When the primary income's pay day or weekend rule is corrected after that month's salary was already due, the current period extends to the following month until the user records what happened; the app asks, offering only the operation that fits and that the database can accept: the early pay date for a new salary (due at least 7 days after the period started), moving the period's start for this period's own salary (due fewer than 7 days after it started), and nothing when neither can be saved.
rules.rationale: Frontend behaviour; the database part is R-PERIOD-029, R-PERIOD-034 and R-PERIOD-012.
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category becomes a group when its first subcategory is created and stays one: a group holds no expectation and takes no transaction, and its expected amount and spending are the sums of its subcategories'.
rules.rationale: Even once its subcategories are gone, a group stays a group (Q-081), so its history never mixes the two shapes.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: A total for a period (expected, left to assign) adds the rounded monthly shares, so what is displayed adds up.
rules.rationale: Example: two yearly amounts of 6 rappen expect 1 + 1 = 2 rappen a month, not 12 / 12 = 1.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: When the first subcategory is added to a category that already has transactions or a non-zero expectation, they move, with every past expectation, to a subcategory created with it (named by the client, shown as "Other"), so no transaction is ever left on a category that has subcategories and no period's totals change.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: A category is created from the current period, or, as an explicit choice, from an earlier period; a subcategory is never in force outside its group.
rules.rationale: Back-dating lets transactions be entered for the periods before the categories were set up (R-PERIOD-016).
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget has at most 200 categories and subcategories in force and 500 in all (void rows, kept only for their transactions, not counted); an expectation amount, per month or per year, is from 0 to CHF 10 million.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Ending a category ends its subcategories with it, within its own validity; a category or subcategory with transactions that would never be in force is kept as a void row, so its transactions still count where they are dated.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Categories are ordered among their siblings; a reorder lists exactly the siblings not ended, and is refused when another member added or removed one meanwhile. Reordering is not an edit of a category.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The budget page lists the categories in force now in their order, each with its amount per month as the database gives it (a yearly amount also as entered), a group with its subcategories and their total, and the current period's income, total planned and amount left to assign, a negative amount shown as assigned beyond the income; removed categories are listed apart.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Before the first subcategory of a category is saved, the app says that the category becomes a group and, when it has an amount or transactions, that they move to a new subcategory "Other"; the translated name of "Other" is always sent with a new subcategory.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Before a category is removed, the app says which of the two will happen, from the database's own answer: deleted (it never counted and has no transactions), no longer planned from the current period with past periods keeping it and its transactions kept, or, when it was added this period and has transactions, kept without an amount; that its subcategories go with it; and it offers removal from an earlier period only as an explicit option with a warning.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A new amount is said to apply from the current period; correcting an earlier period is offered only as an explicit option, off by default, with a warning that past periods change; a group's amount is not editable (it is the total of its subcategories).
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category can be counted from an earlier period and a removed one restored, each said beforehand: counting from an earlier period is an explicit correction that changes those periods' plans and results; restoring plans it again from the current period with nothing expected in the periods between (their totals unchanged), or, as an explicit correction, as if it had never ended (the only way in an ended budget); a subcategory needs its group in force first. A category removed in the period it was added (never planned) is listed among the removed ones while it has transactions and can be restored; one removed from the current period is restored from that period, as if it had never been removed, without a correction to choose. A removed category restored by another member first is said so, and cannot be restored again.
source: owner-request: coordinator, frontend adaptation to the step 3 database review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every editable record has a revision that changes with every change to it; every edit or removal sends the revision the client read and is refused with record_changed when it differs. There are no direct writes.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: An edit form or removal confirmation reads its record by id, never from a list, and saves over the version it opened. When another member changes a field it shows (the save is refused, or a later read shows it), it says so with their values field by field: with nothing typed it takes their version; with something typed it keeps what was typed and lets the user load their version or keep theirs, and keeping theirs saves only the fields they edited. Values that only mean something together (a category's amount and cadence, an income's pay day and weekend rule) are one field throughout: an edit to any part keeps and sends the whole group as the form shows it, and a group not edited takes the other member's version whole (D-160). The note that the form took their version goes once the user types or saves. A change to fields it does not show (the user's own save in another form, another member's change elsewhere) is taken silently. A record deleted meanwhile is said to be gone and cannot be saved; a category ended meanwhile is said to be removed, and one turned into a group meanwhile is said so and only its name can still be saved, with the typed amount named so it is not lost silently.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction is dated from the first period's start to today, and not after the last period's end.
rules.rationale: Not after today, rather than up to the current period's end: a change of the primary income's terms re-projects the current period's end and could otherwise leave a future-dated transaction outside every period (D-145).
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction goes on a category in force in the period containing its date; a back-dated one may use a category that has since ended.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: Money coming in that is neither a salary nor a refund is recorded as an extra income, with a date, an amount and a description and no category; it adds to the income total of the period containing its date and to nothing else.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decisions on the step 3 open questions, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: Transactions follow their date through every boundary operation, and no operation can leave a transaction outside every period.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction amount is from 1 rappen to CHF 10 million, a description at most 500 characters, and a budget holds at most 50 000 transactions.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Each transaction keeps who recorded it; the list is read in pages of at most 200, newest first in a stable order, by a cursor, and can be filtered by dates, category and kind.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The transaction form records an expense, a refund or an extra income (no category); its date is limited to what the database accepts (the first period's start to today, or an ended budget's last day) and today by default; its category choices are read from the database for the date and read again whenever the date changes, a failed read is shown with a retry, and a transaction being edited keeps the category it already has even when that category is no longer planned on its date (shown as such), only while the date stays within the transaction's own period (D-159); moved to another period, a category no longer planned there must be chosen again, and the form says so; "save and add another" keeps the kind, date and category for the next receipt.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The transactions page lists transactions newest first, grouped by day, a page at a time through the database's cursor, once the filters are known; it is filtered by period (the current one by default), category (a group with its subcategories; one without a plan only when a link chose it) and kind, the filters kept in the address; a period or category the budget does not have falls back to all.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The progress of any period, current or past, can be read: per category and subcategory the expectation in force then, what was spent and the result, and the period's income, expected, left to assign, spent and result.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category with transactions dated in a period where it is not in force is shown in that period with nothing expected and its spending counted; what was spent in a category may be negative when refunds exceed expenses.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A period's totals always equal the sum of its progress rows, computed by the same database functions.
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The dashboard shows the progress of one period, the current one by default (the last once the budget has ended): its income, planned, spent and result as a surplus or a deficit, and per category and subcategory what was planned, spent and is left, each figure under its column header, overspending marked by the database's flag and drawn in proportion (the share beyond the plan), not as a full bar; earlier and later periods are browsed in place, the Periods page links each period to its progress, and each category leads to its transactions in that period.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 3 screens, 2026-11-16
owner-request: coordinator, step 3 screens review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Before "this period's salary has not arrived yet" is confirmed, the app lists, from the database's preview, each thing recorded in the period being removed (incomes, and categories in their own words) and what will happen to it (applies to the reopened period, replaces what that period had, or disappears), says when nothing was recorded, and says that recording the salary again later restores the dates only; it cannot be confirmed until that list has been read, and when it cannot be read the dialog says so and offers to read it again.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The app offers "the salary arrived early" and "this period's salary actually arrived on another day" only when some date for it can be saved (every period 7 to 92 days long, an arrival today or earlier and not after the end date entered); otherwise the action is shown unavailable with the reason. Its dialog gives the dates that can work, and a date outside them is neither previewed nor sent. The database still decides.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Every period action sends the period the user was looking at (its id and revision). When the database refuses it because that period changed (another member acted first, or an earlier attempt already went through), the action is closed, the periods are read again and the page says so; nothing is retried automatically. A start set by hand can be moved back to the schedule's day, which clears its "set by hand" mark; when the database refuses that move as an invalid boundary, the confirmation says the schedule's day does not fit between the neighbouring periods (it names no date: Q-091).
source: owner-request: coordinator, frontend adaptation to the step 3 database review fixes, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A boundary operation names the period the client saw (its id and revision) and is refused with record_changed when that period changed or is gone, so a second click, a retry or another member's concurrent action never applies the operation twice.
An existing category can be made to count from an earlier period, as an explicit correction, with its earliest expectation there unless another amount is given; a subcategory never before its group.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: An ended category can be restored: from the current period, expecting nothing in the periods between its end and now, or, as an explicit correction, from the period it ended, as if it had never ended; a subcategory needs its group in force.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: Reading and changing a budget's categories and transactions costs what that budget holds, never what other budgets hold.
A transaction may always keep the category it already has while it stays in the same period; the category must be in force in the period of its date only when the category or the period changes.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: A boundary moved to where the schedule puts it (the previous period's projected end) is not marked as set by hand, and a past boundary can be moved back to the schedule without giving a date.
source: owner-request: project coordinator decision on the step 3 database review, 2026-11-16 (the product owner asked to proceed on the coordinator's defaults)

rules.statement: An income's name and terms are edited in one call, which returns the new revision; terms not given keep their value.
Registering a table for merges is refused unless a validity table's checks on first_seq and end_seq accept a void row and a version table has a foreign key from its entity column to its entity table.
A budget has at most 50 subscriptions in force and 200 in all (void ones not counted); a price is 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen; a schedule date is at most ten years ahead.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16
rules.rationale: Abuse bounds, generous for a household: with them a catch-up after years of absence stays within a few seconds.

rules.statement: A subscription is charged at most once per scheduled date, however many members open the budget at once or retry: a charge deleted or answered as not gone through is never created again, and no edit, correction or reopen creates a charge for a date already passed.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A subscription counts from the start of its first period: its charges due from then up to today are created when it is created (from an earlier period, as an explicit correction, too). Automatic charges count towards the transaction limit; when the budget is full they wait, none skipped, until there is room.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Ending a subscription stops its charges from that period on and keeps it in the past; one that never counted before that period and has no transaction is deleted instead. Its charges are never deleted.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Changing a subscription's schedule from now sets the date of its next charge (after today), and the later ones follow from it at its cadence; a new cadence without a date continues from the next charge of the current schedule.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A budget has at most 50 debts in force and 200 in all (void ones not counted) and 5000 balance adjustments; a principal and a planned payment are at most 1 000 000 000 rappen, a rate 0 to 100 % with at most three decimals, and a remaining amount never grows beyond CHF 10 billion.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16
rules.rationale: Abuse bounds; the balance bound keeps every amount within range however long interest runs.

rules.statement: Interest is applied at most once per debt and period, however many members open the budget at once or retry, and a reopen followed by a new roll-over applies it once again.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The expected end is projected period by period: the planned payment still due in the current period first, then each later period adds its interest and receives the planned payment; beyond 600 periods (50 years) the answer is that the debt never ends.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A reopen that merges a period removes the interest that period added (and the reopen preview says so); removing a debt with history ends it and keeps its payments, interest and adjustments, and its remaining amount.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A debt's principal can be corrected only while it has no payment, interest or adjustment; afterwards its balance is adjusted instead. A correction of its terms from an earlier period never recomputes interest already added.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A transaction linked to a debt or a subscription is an expense; a debt payment is in the debt's category; the debt or subscription is in force in the period of the date, except that a linked transaction keeping its period and category keeps its link.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A category that a subscription or debt in force still uses cannot be removed; one that any subscription or debt references is ended, never deleted; adding its first subcategory moves its subscriptions and debts to "Other" with its transactions.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Subscriptions, debts and their terms take part in a reopen like incomes and categories (what the merged period recorded replaces the reopened period's, and the preview lists it), and a reopen never loses a charge, a payment or an adjustment.
source: owner-request: database developer decision for step 4, within the coordinator's brief, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The subscriptions page lists the subscriptions in force with their price and cadence, category, next charge date, monthly cost and, in words with an icon, how many charges await confirmation; the total committed per month is the current period's committed figure; ended subscriptions are folded away; with none, the page says what subscriptions are for and offers to add one. Every date and figure is the database's.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The subscription form previews the upcoming charge dates as subscription_charge_dates gives them (a new one from the start of the period it counts from, flagging the dates up to today as charged at once; an edit from the new next charge date, from the next charge for a new cadence alone, otherwise the schedule as it stands); an edit says that new terms apply from the current period and past periods keep theirs; a new next charge date from now must be after today; counting from an earlier period is an explicit, warned correction.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A subscription's price, cadence and new next charge date are one field for concurrent edits: shown as one value of the other member's version, kept or taken whole by "Keep mine", and saved together whenever any of them differs.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The transactions list marks automatic charges and, in words with an icon, those awaiting confirmation, and lets a member answer them there as on the dashboard; debt payments name their debt.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Removing a subscription says beforehand, from the database's removal_deletes, whether it is deleted or ended from the current period (its charges kept, those awaiting confirmation still to answer); ending it from an earlier period is an explicit, warned correction.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A debt's interest rate is typed as a percentage, optional, from 0 to 100 with at most three decimals (a comma or a dot), read and checked as a decimal string, never through float arithmetic, and sent exactly as typed.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The debts page shows each debt in force with its remaining amount, how much is paid off (a bar with its figure in words), its planned payment and rate, and the database's projection in words: "Paid off", "Ends around <month year> · N payments left" said to be an estimate, or a "Never ends at this payment" warning with an icon; and the total remaining across the debts in force.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: A debt's page shows its evolution as a step chart of the balance by date, each kind of event with its own mark, and the same history as a table (its text alternative), payments leading to their transactions; it records a payment (the transaction form with the debt and its category chosen), adjusts the balance (the user types the balance the bank shows and is told the database stores the difference), deletes an adjustment (with the debt's revision), edits the debt (its principal only while it has no history) and removes it, saying beforehand whether it is deleted or ended.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: The transaction form offers "This is a payment on …" for an expense in a category that debts in force are paid from; a payment stays an expense; on an existing transaction the link is changed through link_transaction (removed before its fields change, added after), never through update_transaction.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: Removing a category that a subscription or debt in force uses (category_overview.in_use) is not offered: the confirmation says what uses it and where to end or move it.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

rules.statement: What subscriptions commit is shown inside the plan, never added to it: per category on the budget page and in the progress view ("of which … committed"), and for the period with its planned total.
source: owner-request: coordinator brief for the step 4 screens, 2026-11-16

decisions.title: The structured spec is the source of truth
decisions.decision: spec/spec.json holds the glossary, actors, features and user stories, rules, decisions, conventions and open questions. docs/spec.md and the conventions block of CLAUDE.md are generated from it, and npm run spec:check fails when the spec, its tests or its generated views disagree.
decisions.why: Prose cannot be checked; a structured file with ids lets code that breaks a rule be caught early.
rejected: Keeping docs/domain.md as the prose source of truth: readable, but nothing can check it.
Hand-maintained copies of the rules in several files: they drift.

decisions.title: docs/domain.md is the source of truth for product behaviour
decisions.decision: docs/domain.md recorded the product owner's requirements and the decisions taken on top of them, updated when a decision changed.
decisions.why: One readable place for product behaviour.

decisions.title: Static single-page app on Supabase, no custom server
decisions.decision: The app is a static SPA (Vite, React, TypeScript strict, Tailwind, shadcn/ui) that calls Supabase (Postgres, Auth, RLS) directly from the browser with supabase-js. No Node and no PHP at runtime.
decisions.why: Any static host can serve the build, and access control lives in one place: RLS.
rejected: A custom server or API in front of the database.
Running Node or PHP on the hosting.

decisions.title: Infomaniak static hosting with an .htaccess SPA fallback
decisions.decision: dist/ is served as static files by Infomaniak Apache web hosting. public/.htaccess serves index.html for unknown paths, but a missing file under assets/ is a real 404, and every module-specific block is wrapped in <IfModule>.
decisions.why: Deep links and reloads work; serving HTML in place of a missing script would hide the error behind a MIME type failure; a missing module must not turn the site into a 500.
rejected: Serving index.html for missing assets.

decisions.title: Manual deploy workflow, gated by the CI checks
decisions.decision: The Deploy GitHub workflow runs only when started by hand. It checks the variables and the CSP, runs lint, typecheck and tests, builds, and syncs dist/ to the site folder with rsync over SSH. A rollback is a deploy of an earlier ref.
decisions.why: A manual run on a broken ref cannot ship it; the server keeps its .well-known folder.

decisions.title: Migrations go out before the code and stay backwards compatible
decisions.decision: Migrations are pushed to the hosted project before deploying a release that needs them, and are kept compatible with the previous release (add first, remove in a later release), or fixed forward.
decisions.why: The new code never runs against an old schema, and a rollback does not undo migrations.
rejected: Relying on a rollback to undo a migration.

decisions.title: Money is integer rappen
decisions.decision: Amounts are integer rappen (1 CHF = 100 rappen) in the database (bigint) and in code (a safe integer number), and are formatted only at the edge.
decisions.why: Exact arithmetic.
rejected: Floats.

decisions.title: CHF only
decisions.decision: The app handles one currency, the Swiss franc.
decisions.why: A household budget in Switzerland.

decisions.title: Swiss money format, the same in both languages
decisions.decision: Amounts are shown as "CHF 1'234.50" (apostrophe for thousands, dot for rappen, sign before the digits: "CHF -12.00"), whatever the UI language. Input accepts an optional CHF, a sign, ' or ’ or spaces between thousands, a dot or a comma with at most two decimals, and the Swiss ".-" for whole francs.
decisions.why: The source asks for Swiss formatting; one format avoids ambiguity between languages.

decisions.title: Two kinds of date, one formatter each
decisions.decision: Calendar dates (YYYY-MM-DD) and timestamps (with a time and an explicit zone) each have their own formatter, and each rejects the other kind and any invalid input with a RangeError. Typed dates are dd.mm.yyyy, one-digit day and month allowed.
decisions.why: They cannot be mixed up at a call site, and an invalid input never prints a plausible-looking wrong date.
rejected: A single formatter that guesses the kind of value.

decisions.title: Tests run in Europe/Zurich
decisions.decision: Vitest runs with TZ=Europe/Zurich.
decisions.why: A non-UTC zone with summer time makes time-zone shifts visible in tests.
rejected: Running tests in UTC, where shifts go unnoticed.

decisions.title: Auth email links use the implicit flow
decisions.decision: supabase-js is configured with flowType implicit: confirmation and password-reset links carry the session in the URL fragment.
decisions.why: Links then also work when opened in another browser or on another device.
rejected: PKCE: it needs the code verifier stored by the browser that requested the email.

decisions.title: The app reads email links itself and replaces the history entry
decisions.decision: detectSessionInUrl is off. At start-up, before the router or the Supabase client sees the URL, the app takes tokens or errors out of the URL by replacing the current history entry, and the auth bootstrap hands the tokens to supabase-js.
decisions.why: supabase-js clears the fragment with location.hash = "", which pushes a new history entry and leaves the token-bearing URL one Back step away.
rejected: Letting supabase-js detect the session in the URL.

decisions.title: Recovery mode is tied to one sign-in
decisions.decision: The recovery flag in localStorage names the user and the session key of the sign-in the recovery link created; recovery mode is active only while that exact session is current. Tabs learn of changes through the storage event.
decisions.why: It never applies to another user, nor to the same user after a fresh password sign-in, and a leftover flag is inert even before it is cleaned up. Every tab sharing the session sees it.
rejected: A flag that is not tied to one sign-in, which would hold another user or a later password sign-in on the form.

decisions.title: Undecided link tokens are parked for one tab
decisions.decision: Until the bootstrap has a definite answer for link tokens, they are kept in sessionStorage (this tab only, never in a URL or history entry), for at most 24 hours, together with the session key current when they were parked. A reload retries them only if nobody signed in or out in between.
decisions.why: A network failure while validating a link must not burn it.
rejected: Dropping the link on a network failure.
Keeping the tokens in the URL.

decisions.title: Session identity from the unverified session_id claim
decisions.decision: A sign-in is identified by the session_id claim of its access token (stable across refreshes, new with every sign-in), or by the user id when there is none. The token payload is decoded without verifying its signature.
decisions.why: It is used only to tell sessions apart in this browser, never to grant access: the server checks every request.

decisions.title: Clear the query cache when the user changes
decisions.decision: The TanStack Query cache is cleared whenever the signed-in user changes, including sign-out.
decisions.why: Never show one user's cached data to another.

decisions.title: Zod runs jitless
decisions.decision: z.config({ jitless: true }) runs before any schema is parsed.
decisions.why: The production CSP forbids eval; Zod's probe for new Function is caught, but the browser still reports a CSP violation.
rejected: Zod's default probe and compiled parsers.

decisions.title: Validation messages are translation keys
decisions.decision: Form schemas return translation keys; forms translate them when rendering. Passwords need 8 characters, display names at most 80.
decisions.why: The language can change while an error is shown.

decisions.title: Language detection
decisions.decision: The UI language is the stored choice, else the browser language, reduced to en or fr ("fr-CH" -> "fr"), with English as the fallback. French text uses a narrow no-break space before ? ! : and ;.
decisions.why: Respect an explicit choice, then the browser.

decisions.title: Email confirmation stays on in production
decisions.decision: Email confirmation is kept on for production, with a custom SMTP server for real use.
decisions.why: The free tier sender sends only a few emails per hour.

decisions.title: Narrow connect-src to the project, checked at deploy
decisions.decision: The CSP connect-src should list only the project URL (https and wss); the Deploy workflow stops before building when VITE_SUPABASE_URL is not allowed by connect-src, and checks the policy that actually ships.
decisions.why: The browser may only talk to origins the CSP allows.

decisions.title: Domain logic is pure and unit-tested in the client
decisions.decision: Period, pay-date and versioning logic is pure and unit-tested.
decisions.why: Testable logic.

decisions.title: Domain logic has one implementation, in the database
decisions.decision: Period, pay-date and versioning logic has one implementation, in the database (SQL functions, tested with pgTAP). The client reads the results; it never recomputes them.
decisions.why: One implementation cannot disagree with itself; the database must enforce the invariants anyway.
rejected: A second implementation in the client (D-023).

decisions.title: Periods are numbered; versions refer to period numbers
decisions.decision: Periods are numbered per budget (seq 1, 2, ...). Income validity (first_seq, end_seq) and versions (effective_from_seq) refer to seq, not to dates. An income counts in period p when first_seq <= p and (end_seq is null or p < end_seq), at the version with the greatest effective_from_seq <= p.
decisions.why: Moving a period boundary never changes which version applies.
rejected: Versions effective from a date.

decisions.title: "Today" comes from one database function
decisions.decision: A database function returns the Europe/Zurich calendar date; it is the only source of the current date, and the browser never sends "today". Tests pin it by replacing the function inside their transaction.
decisions.why: One clock for every rule that depends on the date.
rejected: The browser's clock.
UTC.

decisions.title: Writes go through RPCs with stable error codes
decisions.decision: Writes that touch several rows or carry invariants go through security definer RPCs that check membership themselves. The client writes directly only budgets.name and incomes.name (members) and deletes budgets and invitations (owner). RPC errors are SQLSTATE P0001 with a stable snake_case message that the client maps to translated text.
decisions.why: Invariants are enforced in one place; the client can translate every error.

decisions.title: Not found, never forbidden
decisions.decision: A request for a budget, income, period or invitation the caller cannot see is answered as not found; reads of rows outside one's budgets return no rows, never an error.
decisions.why: Non-members cannot tell a budget they may not see from one that does not exist.

decisions.title: Limits
decisions.decision: At most 20 owned budgets per user, 20 members per budget, 20 pending invitations per budget, 50 incomes per budget (ended ones included). Income amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen. A budget starts at most 60 months back; an end date at most ten years ahead; a period is never empty and at most 70 days long. The limits are defined in one place in the migration.
decisions.why: Bound the work of every RPC and keep abuse cheap.

decisions.title: An income that never counted is deleted, not ended
decisions.decision: Removing an income deletes it if it never counted in a past period, and otherwise ends it from the current period. The same applies to the incomes of a member who is removed or leaves.
decisions.why: An income added by mistake leaves no trace; history is kept otherwise.

decisions.title: The primary income also blocks leaving
decisions.decision: A member whose income is the primary income can neither be removed nor leave until another income is made primary.
decisions.why: The budget must keep a primary income.

decisions.title: An end date snaps forward to a period end
decisions.decision: Setting an end date moves it forward to the end of the period that contains it, projected with the primary income's current terms. Clearing it resumes period generation. An end date that would delete existing periods is refused, and a boundary that is the budget's end date is changed through the end date.
decisions.why: The end date always falls on a period boundary without deleting history.

decisions.title: Invitations are idempotent per address
decisions.decision: Inviting the same address again returns the same invitation; addresses are stored lower case; inviting a member's address is refused (already_member).
decisions.why: Members' emails are visible to the owner anyway, so already_member reveals nothing new.

decisions.title: Database conventions
decisions.decision: Functions the API must not call live in the private schema, which the Data API does not expose. Functions use search_path = '' and schema-qualified names. Privileges are granted explicitly (auto_expose_new_tables = false): revoke everything from the API roles, then grant only what the policies allow. Policies call (select auth.uid()).
decisions.why: Nothing is exposed by accident, and auth.uid() is evaluated once per statement.

decisions.title: Shared membership helpers
decisions.decision: Policies use private.member_budget_ids() and private.owned_budget_ids() as `budget_id in (select ...)`; the helpers are security definer.
decisions.why: The helper runs once per statement and never re-enters the policies of budget_members (no recursion).
rejected: Re-deriving membership in every policy.

decisions.title: Invariants are constraint triggers checked at commit
decisions.decision: Invariants (owner is a member, primary income is active, every income has a version from its first period, periods numbered and contiguous up to the end date) are constraint triggers checked at commit.
decisions.why: Multi-row RPCs can pass through intermediate states.

decisions.title: Period creation is serialised per budget
decisions.decision: Every function that creates or moves periods first locks the budget row; ensure_periods is idempotent and safe under concurrent calls.
decisions.why: Concurrent callers run one after the other and cannot create duplicate periods.

decisions.title: Deferred: 13th salary and one-off incomes
decisions.decision: Incomes are monthly for now; a 13th salary or a one-off income comes later.
decisions.why: Not needed for the first version.

decisions.title: Deferred: per-category rollover
decisions.decision: Category balances reset at the end of each period; per-category rollover may come later as an opt-in.
decisions.why: Keep the first version simple.

decisions.title: No bank connection; actuals may be overlaid later
decisions.decision: The money flow diagram is drawn from the plan. The app has no bank connection, so it does not depend on detecting automatic transactions. Actuals may be overlaid later.
decisions.why: No bank integration.
rejected: Detecting automatic transactions from a bank feed.
source: domain: Account and planned transfer (money flow)

decisions.title: Deferred: import from a connector
decisions.decision: Import is reachable from a paste/CSV screen and a repository script first, and later from a connector.
decisions.why: Ship the two paths that need no extra integration first.
source: domain: Import (including by a Claude session)

decisions.title: Temporary "test pending" marker for untagged database tests
decisions.decision: A rule or convention whose proof lives in supabase/tests may carry a visible testPending marker until those tests are tagged with ids. spec:check reports every marker as a warning, with a count, and errors on a marker anywhere else (planned rule, enforcement other than test).
decisions.why: The database tests were being edited by another developer when the spec was introduced; the check must pass without silently passing or weakening those rules.
rejected: Silently treating untagged rules as covered.
Downgrading them to enforcement review.

decisions.title: Profiles are created by a database trigger
decisions.decision: A trigger on auth.users creates the profile at sign-up from the display name sent as sign-up metadata. Clients cannot insert or delete profiles; deleting the user cascades.
decisions.why: Every user has a profile without a client round trip.

decisions.title: Deploying in a subfolder
decisions.decision: VITE_BASE_PATH sets both Vite's base and the router basename at build time; .htaccess works out the base path itself.
decisions.why: The same build works at a domain root or in a subfolder.

decisions.title: Members manage every income of the budget
decisions.decision: Any member of a budget can add, edit and remove any income in that budget, including one belonging to another member. A new income belongs to the member who adds it by default; the form lets them choose another member. Decided by the product owner on 2026-11-15.
decisions.why: It matches "every member can read and edit everything in the budget" and what the database already does.
rejected: Members can only add and edit their own incomes.
source: owner-request: product owner decision on Q-001, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The current budget is a per-user browser preference
decisions.decision: The budget a user works in is kept in localStorage under a key that names the user; when it is missing or no longer in my_budgets, the first budget by name is used (and not stored until the user chooses). my_budgets is refetched on window focus and after any "not found" answer. Users without a budget are routed to /welcome; app pages require a budget.
decisions.why: Reloads keep the choice, two people sharing a browser keep their own, and a budget that disappears is replaced at once.
rejected: Storing the choice in the database: a per-browser convenience, not budget data.
Putting the budget id in every URL: longer links and more routing for a household app.

decisions.title: One mutation pattern with one error mapping
decisions.decision: Writes go through useAppMutation: pending state, a translated success toast, the error either inline (forms, dialogs) or as a toast (one-click actions), and invalidation of the affected queries (everything of a budget sits under ["budget", id]). Errors are mapped in src/lib/db-errors.ts only, with a generic translated fallback, and a call may word some codes its own way (for example "already deleted" for delete_budget); the list of codes is checked against the contract's error table; a "not found" answer is always toasted and refetches my budgets.
decisions.why: Later features copy one pattern; a new error code is one line plus its two translations.

decisions.title: Day N of M uses the browser's date, display only
decisions.decision: The dashboard's "day N of M" counts calendar days from the current period's start to the browser's local date, clamped to the period. Which period is current, its dates and its totals come from the database. To be replaced if the contract provides today (Q-016).
decisions.why: The contract gives no "today"; the number is cosmetic and never sent back.

decisions.title: One period per calendar month
decisions.decision: Each period belongs to one calendar month (periods.month) and starts on that month's salary (anchor_date, the scheduled actual pay date). Consecutive periods have consecutive months. A period's projected end is the day before the actual pay date of the next month's nominal pay day under the terms in force for the next period. A mid-period change of the primary's pay day or weekend rule therefore applies to the next month's pay date.
decisions.why: An early salary, a close-by nominal date or a pay-day change could otherwise cut a period short and count a month's salary twice.
rejected: Projecting the end from the first pay date after the period start: an early salary created a 2-day period and a second salary in the same month (review finding 1).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: A manual boundary lies within 14 days of its salary
decisions.decision: A boundary set by hand must leave the next period starting within 14 days of the scheduled pay date of its month. This bound replaces the 70-day period length limit as the abuse limit.
decisions.why: It covers public holidays and late or early salaries, and stops repeated early closes from creating periods without salaries.
rejected: A maximum period length of 70 days: allowed several 1-day periods each with the full income.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: No period starts after today
decisions.decision: Periods exist only up to the one containing today. Moving the boundary before the latest period to today or later means the salary has not arrived yet: the latest period is removed and the previous one is current again with that end. Moving any earlier boundary to today or later is refused.
decisions.why: A future period made an earlier one current again and let an edit be written to a closed period while the next one kept stale terms (review finding 2).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Every manual boundary operation has an inverse
decisions.decision: move_period_boundary(period, null) resets the boundary after a period to the schedule; any move can be moved back. Closing a period early is undone by moving or resetting that boundary, which removes the period started early if its salary is still to come.
decisions.why: One-way operations any member can trigger turn a mistake into permanent damage.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Writing a version discards later versions
decisions.decision: Writing a version for period s deletes the versions of the same entity keyed to later periods, through one generic trigger (private.discard_later_versions) that every versioned table (incomes now; categories, subscriptions and debts later) uses.
decisions.why: A version left for a later period (after a late salary removed that period) would otherwise shadow the edit just saved.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Explicit corrections of the past are allowed, implicit ones never
decisions.decision: Normal edits and removals apply from the current period. update_income_terms and remove_income take an optional from-period (default current) so a mistake, including a back-dated one, can be corrected or the income removed from the period it started in (which deletes it).
decisions.why: A back-dated typo otherwise stayed in every past total for good (review finding 3a).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Limits (revised)
decisions.decision: At most 20 owned budgets per user, 20 members per budget, 20 pending (unexpired) invitations per budget, 50 incomes in force and 500 incomes in all per budget. Income amounts from 1 to 1 000 000 000 rappen. A budget starts at most 60 months back; an end date at most ten years ahead. A manual boundary lies within 14 days of its salary (D-061). The limits are defined in one place in the migration.
decisions.why: Counting ended incomes made the income limit a lifetime limit (review finding 3b); the period-length limit did not stop abuse (D-061).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The end date is a final month
decisions.decision: A budget stores its final month (end_month). Setting an end date picks the month whose period contains it; the end date shown is that period's end (projected while it does not exist), so it follows later changes of the terms and is always a normal boundary. The final boundary is adjusted like any other, in one call. An end date that would delete existing periods is refused.
decisions.why: A stored end date became a stub period with a full month's income when the terms changed (review finding 10).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Invitations expire and name the inviter
decisions.decision: Invitations expire 30 days after they were last sent; re-inviting renews the same invitation. list_my_invitations returns the inviter's name and email. Invitation security depends on Supabase Auth "Confirm email" staying on in the hosted project (docs/deployment.md).
decisions.why: A display name is chosen by its owner and proves nothing; an invitation should not stay valid for ever.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Budget writes take an advisory lock; reads take none
decisions.decision: Every RPC that changes a budget's periods, incomes or members takes a transaction-level advisory lock for the budget and only then reads the rows it checks. ensure_periods and get_current_period take no lock when there is nothing to create. Accepting an invitation locks the invitation row.
decisions.why: A row lock on the budget blocked page loads behind any transaction inserting rows of the budget (review finding 6); reading before locking gave raw errors and let a cancelled invitation be accepted (findings 4 and 7).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: The database gives "today" and the start months
decisions.decision: period_summaries (and so get_current_period) carry the database's today; get_today() returns it on its own; get_start_months(pay day, weekend rule) returns today and the valid start months with the date each first period would start.
decisions.why: The client must never use the browser's clock for what the database decides (Q-016).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: create_budget takes the end date
decisions.decision: create_budget has an optional end date, applied in the same transaction.
decisions.why: A second call could fail and leave a budget without the end date the user asked for (Q-017).
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: Deletes go through RPCs that say why
decisions.decision: Deleting a budget and cancelling an invitation are RPCs (delete_budget, cancel_invitation) that answer budget_not_found / invitation_not_found or not_owner; the client has no direct delete privilege on these tables.
decisions.why: A direct delete affecting no rows cannot tell "not allowed" from "already gone".
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

decisions.title: A manual end survives a terms change only within 14 days
decisions.decision: When the primary's terms change or the primary is switched, a manual end of the current period is kept while it lies within 14 days of the new schedule, and reset to the schedule otherwise.
decisions.why: Keeping it unconditionally would let the next period start more than 14 days from its salary (D-061).
rejected: Refusing the terms change: blocks the user for a boundary they may have forgotten.
