openQuestions.question: Should the database return "today" (or the day number within the current period) so that the client never uses the browser's date?
openQuestions.context: The dashboard shows "day N of M" of the current period; the contract returns the period but not the Europe/Zurich date the database decided it with, so N comes from the browser (D-048) and can differ around midnight or in another time zone.

openQuestions.question: Should create_budget take the end date, so that a budget with an end date is created in one atomic step?
openQuestions.context: The first-run form asks for an optional end date; create_budget has no such argument, so the client calls set_budget_end_date afterwards. If that second call fails, the budget exists without its end date and the user is told so.

openQuestions.question: What should happen to a budget and its incomes when a member's or the owner's account is deleted?
openQuestions.context: No client path deletes accounts yet. Today, deleting the owner's account deletes their budgets for every member (R-BUDGET-016), and deleting a member's account keeps their incomes with a null owner without the member rules: an income that is primary stays active and primary (review finding 8). Settle before any account-deletion feature.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the step 2 database review, 2026-11-15

openQuestions.question: When two members edit the same income at the same time, should the second save be refused (for example with a version check) instead of silently overwriting the first?
openQuestions.context: Today the last write wins without a warning: update_income_terms and the rename both replace what is there. Every member can edit every income (D-045), so two members of a household can edit the same salary from two browsers.

openQuestions.question: How is a half rappen rounded when one twelfth (or another monthly share) falls exactly between two rappen, and do the totals (left to assign, results, committed amounts) add up the rounded monthly shares or round the exact sum?
openQuestions.context: D-100 says one twelfth rounded to the nearest rappen. A yearly amount that is 6 rappen more than a multiple of 12 gives exactly half a rappen (CHF 1.50 a year gives 12.5 rappen), and the tie rule is not given. D-110 also needs a monthly cost for quarterly, half-yearly and yearly subscriptions; the answers do not say it uses the same rounding.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: What happens to the transactions already on a category when the user adds its first subcategory?
openQuestions.context: D-102: when a category has subcategories, a transaction goes on a subcategory, never on the parent. A category without subcategories holds transactions directly, so adding a subcategory later would leave them on the parent (they could be moved, refused, or kept for past periods only).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: How is money coming in that is neither a salary nor a refund (a gift, a resale, a reimbursement from a third party) recorded?
openQuestions.context: Q-004 asked about extra income; D-102 answers spending and refunds only. Incomes are monthly, and one-off incomes are deferred (D-038).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Can a transaction be added to, or moved into, a category that has ended, when its date falls in a period where the category was still in force?
openQuestions.context: D-105 lets transactions in past periods be added and edited freely; D-107 ends a deleted category from the current period while past periods keep it.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When are automatic subscription charges created, given that there is no server: are charge dates missed while nobody opened the app created later, back-dated, and is a charge whose transaction was deleted or answered "did not go through" ever created again?
openQuestions.context: D-109: the transaction is created on the charge date, can be deleted, and is removed when the user says it did not go through. The app is a static SPA on Supabase (D-003), so creation can only happen when the database is next called. Also open: whether editing the subscription (a new version) changes charges already created.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: When in a period is a debt's interest applied (at its start or end, before or after that period's payments), how is it rounded to the rappen, and does a payment exactly equal to the interest count as "never ends"?
openQuestions.context: D-113: once per period, one twelfth of the yearly rate is applied to the remaining balance and added to it; when the planned payment does not cover the interest the app says the debt never ends. Periods run salary to salary, not by calendar month (D-080), and the expected end date needs a date for each future interest step.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Are identical rows within the same file duplicates of each other, are refunds and manually entered transactions compared too, and is "import anyway" chosen per row or for all skipped rows?
openQuestions.context: D-115 compares an imported row with existing transactions. Two identical purchases on one day (two coffees) appear as two identical rows in one export; the answer does not say whether the second is skipped.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: What identifies a merchant for a merchant-to-category rule: the whole description, a part of it, or a field of the bank export?
openQuestions.context: D-117 offers "always put this merchant in this category?". Bank descriptions often carry a date, a card number or a location around the merchant name, so an exact match on the description would rarely match again. The sample statements show that the bank cuts merchant names at 24 characters, that one merchant can be printed in different capitals or with different processor prefixes, and that chains add a branch number (docs/import-sources.md). The card bill adds a merchant category line.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Which product is "One", what export formats do Migros Bank, Raiffeisen, One, Yuh and Twint actually offer, and can the product owner provide sample export files?
openQuestions.context: D-119 asks for presets for these five sources. "One" may be Viseca's "one" credit-card portal; that is unconfirmed. Twint may offer no export at all. Sample export files are needed before the presets can be built.
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: For a planned transfer on a fixed day of the month, is the day clamped to the month's length and does a weekend rule apply; may a pay-date offset be negative; and what happens to a transfer whose chosen income ends?
openQuestions.context: D-120 allows an offset in days from a chosen income's actual pay date, or a fixed day of the month. Subscriptions clamp and use no weekend rule (D-108), but nothing says the same for transfers. An income ends when it is removed or its member leaves (R-MEMBER-007).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: On which date is the transaction of an automatic transfer linked to a category created, does it wait for confirmation like a subscription charge, and does unmarking a manual transfer as done remove its transaction?
openQuestions.context: D-122: when a transfer linked to a category is marked done, or when it is automatic, its transaction is created in that category. Automatic transfers are assumed done (R-ACCOUNT-004); subscription charges, also automatic, wait for confirmation (D-109).
source: owner-request: product owner decisions on the open questions, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should an edit be able to apply from the next period ("from the next salary") instead of the current one?
openQuestions.context: An edit always applies to the current period (R-VERSION-001), so a raise entered before its salary arrives changes the current period's total. A later option could key the edit to the next period, which needs a way to hold a change for a period that does not exist yet without breaking "nothing keyed beyond the latest period" (R-VERSION-011).
source: owner-request: coordinator decision on the third step 2 database review, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should a category's expectation be scaled for a period much longer or shorter than a month, such as a reopened period of 60 to 92 days?
openQuestions.context: Each expectation counts once per period, like an income (D-147, R-INCOME-011). A reopened period (R-PERIOD-023) can last up to 92 days and still expects one month of each category, while two months of spending land in it.

openQuestions.question: Should a category whose subcategories have all been deleted become an ordinary category again, able to hold an expectation and transactions?
openQuestions.context: D-141: a category stays a group once it had a subcategory, so an empty group expects nothing and takes no transaction until a subcategory is added.

openQuestions.question: Should an ended category be restorable (in force again from the current period) instead of being created anew?
openQuestions.context: Ending is final today (R-CATEGORY-072); a new category with the same name starts a new history, so past periods and the new one show two separate rows.

openQuestions.question: Are future-dated transactions needed (a bill known in advance), and if so how should they behave when the period they fall in has not started yet?
openQuestions.context: D-145 limits dates to today. Planned recurring charges are subscriptions (step 4), whose charges are created on the charge date (D-109).
source: owner-request: project coordinator brief for the step 3 database, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should two members reordering the same categories at the same time be detected, like other concurrent edits?
openQuestions.context: A reorder is refused when the set of categories changed meanwhile (R-CATEGORY-096), but two reorders of the same set: the later wins. Ordering is not a revision of a category (D-142), so a reorder never blocks another member's edit.

openQuestions.question: Will any member import statements in German, Italian or English, and can the product owner provide a sample of each?
openQuestions.context: D-134 supports the French versions first. The labels, and possibly the date and number formats, differ in other languages; each language needs a sample before its parser can be tested.
source: owner-request: coordinator decisions on the sample statements for the import, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Do Migros Bank e-banking and Yuh also offer a CSV or camt.053 export of the same transactions, and should the import prefer it to the PDF?
openQuestions.context: A structured export would be sturdier than reading a PDF layout, which the banks can change without notice. The samples provided are PDF only.

openQuestions.question: How is a transfer to another member of the household treated, for example a standing order to a partner at the same address: an expense, a transfer between the household's accounts, or something else?

openQuestions.question: What exactly is remembered when the user imports or skips a flagged entry: the choice per kind of entry, per counterparty or per account, and for the whole budget or for the member only?

openQuestions.question: When does a salary credit match one of the budget's incomes: same amount, same payer, a date near the expected pay date, or a combination; and what happens when the amount differs from the planned income?
openQuestions.context: D-130 skips a salary credit that matches an income. The Migros Bank statement marks it "Paiement de salaire" with the employer's name, but gives no reference to the income.

openQuestions.question: When a credit is reviewed as a refund, in which period and category does it count, and can it reduce a category below zero?
openQuestions.context: D-130 proposes other credits as a refund in a category or as extra income. TWINT money received from a person is often a share of a bill paid earlier, possibly in another period.

openQuestions.question: Should regular investment purchases (a savings plan) count as spending in the period, or as savings that the money flow of step 7 shows as a transfer?
openQuestions.context: D-131 imports them as ordinary transactions until accounts exist. On the Yuh statement a purchase is a debit like any other, with the security, quantity, price and fees on its continuation lines.

openQuestions.question: How is an imported card or bank line reconciled with a transaction already in the budget for the same charge, such as an automatic subscription charge or a manually entered expense?
openQuestions.context: R-IMPORT-070 treats a row as a duplicate only when date, amount and description are the same; a statement line has the bank's description and often a different date (D-128), so the same charge would be counted twice.

openQuestions.question: Are cash withdrawals expenses when they are made, or transfers to a cash wallet whose spending is entered by hand?

openQuestions.question: Does the household have other cards or accounts to import, such as a partner's card, a supplementary card on the same card account, or another member's Yuh account, and should each import be tied to one of the budget's accounts?

openQuestions.question: Should a past boundary moved by hand and then moved back to where the projection put it stop being marked "set by hand"?
openQuestions.context: move_period_start and record_early_pay_date always set periods.end_is_manual = true, also when the date goes back to its original day, and the contract has no way to clear the mark on a past period (set_expected_pay_date resets only the current period's end). The client cannot tell a past boundary that matches the schedule (C-LOGIC-003). The periods page now explains on the badge that the mark stays after moving back. Options: the database clears end_is_manual when a boundary is moved back to its projected date, or the mark is dropped for past periods.
source: owner-request: coordinator, step 2 browser review fixes, 2026-11-16

openQuestions.question: Should add_transaction take a client-generated id, so that a double-submitted or retried save records the transaction once?
openQuestions.context: The boundary operations name the period they act on (D-151), so a retry is refused; an add has no record to name yet. The review recorded a double-submitted add_transaction as two rows. The screens disable the button while saving, but a retry after a lost response would still record twice.

openQuestions.question: Should the database say where the schedule would put a period's start, and whether moving it back there would be accepted?
openQuestions.context: "Move this period's start back to the schedule" calls move_period_start without a date; the client cannot know the schedule's day (C-LOGIC-003), so the confirmation names no date and the action is offered even when the database will refuse it (invalid_boundary), which the dialog then says. Options: a period_summaries.scheduled_start column (null when it equals the start), or preview_move_period_start(p_period_id) returning the scheduled date and whether it fits between the neighbouring periods, so the action is offered only when it can work and names its date.

openQuestions.question: When the transaction limit holds automatic charges back, should the app tell the members?

openQuestions.question: Should a price change also update the charges already created and still awaiting confirmation?

openQuestions.question: Should an old charge awaiting confirmation be confirmed automatically after some time?

openQuestions.question: Should the database give the total remaining across a budget's debts?

openQuestions.question: Should the transaction form also link a transaction to a subscription (a charge recorded by hand)?
